geopolitics_summary: Iran sanctions reimposed; Russia refinery strikes intensify; EU-Russia energy ties under pressure amid Ukraine conflict.

themes.headline: Trump administration reimposes sanctions on Iranian oil sales
themes.why_it_matters: Reduced Iran supply tightens global crude; higher Brent props up European gas switching (fuel-switching arbitrage via crude-TTF linkage). Higher crude → higher thermal power generation costs.

themes.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's largest oil refinery near Omsk
themes.why_it_matters: Damage to Russian refining capacity reduces fuel supply flexibility and may force Russian crude onto export market. Tightens European fuel supply and elevates thermal generation costs via crude-TTF coupling.

themes.headline: EU shipyard races to service Russia's LNG fleet before sanctions
themes.why_it_matters: Imminent EU sanctions on Russian LNG maintenance could curtail Gazprom LNG availability to global markets. Lower non-EU LNG supply may ease marginal cost for NW Europe LNG arb and lower TTF; bullish-gas (bearish-power).

themes.headline: Belgium heat wave kills 1,200; emergency infrastructure under scrutiny
themes.why_it_matters: Extreme heat drives peak demand for cooling; cooling load on European grid spikes. Higher peak demand increases day-ahead power spreads and forward curve risk, especially for summer Cal+1 contracts.

themes.headline: U.S. refining capacity decreased 1% in 2025 versus 2024
themes.why_it_matters: Slower US refining capacity growth may tighten global refined products and limit US export supply. Indirect: props Brent and crude-TTF spread; affects EU thermal generation cost, but magnitude and timing unclear.

watchlist: EU sanctions implementation on Russian LNG servicing—watch for enforcement date and shipyard closure.
